title.rendered: The High Priestly Prayer | Teach Me How to Pray, Day 12

excerpt.rendered: The upper room. The last night before the cross. Jesus lifted His eyes to heaven and prayed the longest recorded prayer of His earthly ministry. He prayed for you by name in essence.

content.rendered:
The upper room. The last night before the cross. Jesus lifted His eyes to heaven and prayed the longest recorded prayer of His earthly ministry. He prayed for Himself. Then for the eleven. Then for every believer who would come after them. He prayed for you by name, in essence, in that prayer.

The Gospel For Today | Wednesday, October 14, 2026 | Teach Me How to Pray, Day 12

Today’s Scripture

“I do not pray for these alone, but also for those who will believe in Me through their word; that they all may be one, as You, Father, are in Me, and I in You; that they also may be one in Us, that the world may believe that You sent Me.”
John 17:20-21 (NKJV)

Today’s Message

In the upper room in Jerusalem, on the last night of His earthly life, after the foot-washing and the farewell discourse, Jesus lifted His eyes to heaven and prayed the longest recorded prayer of His entire ministry. John 17 preserves it in full. It is called the High Priestly Prayer because in it, Jesus functioned as the great High Priest, interceding before the Father on behalf of His people. The prayer is in three movements. First, Jesus prayed for Himself and for the glory of the Father to be revealed through the hours of the cross that lay ahead. Second, He prayed for the eleven disciples sitting with Him in the upper room, that they would be kept, sanctified, and sent into the world. And third, in the longest and most tender movement of the prayer, He prayed for everyone who would ever believe in Him through the message those eleven men would carry.

That third movement is where every modern believer finds themselves in the words of Jesus. “I do not pray for these alone, but also for those who will believe in Me through their word.” This is you. This is me. This is every Christian in Lagos, London, Manila, Nairobi, Sao Paulo, and every other city where the gospel has been preached in the two thousand years since the upper room. Jesus prayed, specifically, for every one of us. He prayed for our unity. He prayed for our oneness with the Father. He prayed that the world would believe through our visible love for one another. He prayed, in essence, for your Christian life today. That is not a decorative truth. It is the foundation of your prayer life, because the One you are praying to is the One who already prayed for you.

The Passion Translation captures the depth of what Jesus asked for: “And I ask not only for these disciples, but also for all those who will one day believe in me through their message. I pray for them all to be joined together as one even as you and I, Father, are joined together as one. I pray for them to become one with us so that the world will recognise that you sent me” (John 17:20-21 TPT). The Amplified Bible Classic Edition adds: “Neither for these alone do I pray [it is not for their sake only that I make this request], but also for all those who will ever come to believe in (trust, cling to, rely on) Me through their word and teaching” (John 17:20 AMPC). All those who will ever come to believe. Jesus prayed for you by anticipation, before you were born, on the night before He died.

How Jesus Prayed

The Format. Three concentric circles. For Himself first, briefly. For the eleven in the room with Him. For all the believers who would come after. The format trains the believer in intercessory prayer. Begin with your own alignment with the Father, then widen to those immediately in your care, then widen again to the body of Christ across the earth.

The Essence. Jesus prayed for people. Not for things. Not for events. For people. For their unity. For their protection. For their sanctification. For their joy. For the Father’s name to be known in them. Intercessory prayer, modelled by Jesus, is always ultimately about the formation of people in the Father’s purposes.

The Authority. This is high-priestly authority. Jesus prayed as the One standing between heaven and earth, offering the needs of His people before the Father. The believer, as a member of the royal priesthood (1 Peter 2:9), shares in that intercessory role. The authority to pray for others — for their healing, their salvation, their protection, their calling — flows from the believer’s identity as a priest of the New Covenant.

The Assurance. Jesus prayed with total confidence that the Father would answer. He did not plead. He did not persuade. He declared what He was asking for and knew it was granted. “Father, I desire that they also whom You gave Me may be with Me where I am” (John 17:24). “I desire.” Not “I hope.” The intercessor who knows the Father’s heart intercedes from assurance.

The Submission. The entire prayer is framed by the glory of the Father. “Glorify Your Son, that Your Son also may glorify You.” Jesus did not pray for the believers’ comfort. He prayed for their alignment with the Father’s purposes, so that the world would believe. Intercessory prayer always submits the ones being prayed for to the Father’s agenda for them, not the intercessor’s.

The Result. Two thousand years of answered prayer, running through the whole history of the church. Every believer who has ever come to faith is a direct answer to the prayer Jesus prayed that night. For Gospelbuzz readers today, wherever you are reading this from, in Lagos or London or Manila or Nairobi or Sao Paulo, you are living inside the answer to a prayer Jesus prayed in the upper room before you were born. And He has placed on you the same intercessory role. Lift your eyes to heaven today and pray for those under your care — your family, your church, your city, the believers who will come after you. You are a priest in the royal priesthood. Intercede.

Prayer (Pattern After Jesus)

Address. Father, I thank You that Jesus is my great High Priest, ever living to make intercession for me. I come into Your presence today as part of a royal priesthood, authorised to intercede for others as He intercedes for me.

For Myself. Keep me in Your word today. Sanctify me by the truth. Let Your glory be revealed in my life.

For Those In My Care. I lift up [name specific people — family members, close friends, church community]. Keep them. Protect them. Sanctify them. Fulfil Your calling on their lives. Let them be one in You.

For the Wider Body. I pray for the church in [name a specific place or situation]. Let unity, love, and gospel-advance mark Your people in this hour.

Submission. That the world may believe You sent Jesus. Not for my glory. For Yours.

In Jesus’ name. Amen.

Declaration

I am a priest in the royal priesthood of Christ. I intercede for those under my care with the same authority Jesus modelled in John 17. My prayers for others are heard, answered, and effective, because the great High Priest is praying with me and through me.
